title: Health & the Human Body — Simple Science for Primary Students (Love To Teach Primary)

overview.description: A 35-page human body unit covering 6 internal organs: Brain, Heart, Lungs, Stomach, Intestines, Kidneys. Each organ follows an identical multi-page structure: (1) draw the organ on a body outline (small reference image + large blank body), (2) factual information pages, (3) fill-in-the-blank cloze with Word Box. Consistent format means the child knows what to expect for each organ — learns the content, not the format.

perOrganStructure.page1: Title + 'Draw your [organ] on the body below.' Small reference image showing where the organ is located. Large blank body outline for drawing.
perOrganStructure.page2plus: Factual information about the organ: what it does, interesting facts (e.g., 'The small intestine is about 23 feet long in adults').
perOrganStructure.lastPage: Fill-in-the-blank cloze passage with Word Box containing answer choices. Tests comprehension of the facts from the previous pages.

drawOnBodyOutline.description: A blank human body outline with the prompt 'Draw your [organ] on the body below.' A small reference image in the corner shows the correct location. The child draws the organ in the right position. This is ACTIVE learning — they have to think about WHERE the organ goes, not just read about it.
drawOnBodyOutline.value: Spatial reasoning + recall. Drawing from reference = deeper processing than just reading. Also: the child creates a visual artifact they can reference later.

consistentOrganTemplate.description: Every organ follows the EXACT same multi-page structure: draw → read facts → fill in blanks. The child learns the format once and then focuses purely on content for each new organ.
consistentOrganTemplate.value: Reduces cognitive load. Same format, different content = the child gets faster and more confident with each organ.

clozeWithWordBox.description: Fill-in-the-blank sentences with a Word Box containing all answers. 'Your intestines carry out the food after it leaves your _____.' Word Box: 23, waste, stomach, nutrients, 5, colon, guts. The child reads the sentence, identifies the missing word, and selects from the bank.
clozeWithWordBox.value: Reading comprehension + vocabulary application. The Word Box provides scaffolding — the child isn't generating answers from nothing, but they still have to understand the sentence to pick the right word.

gaps.name: body-system-unit
gaps.description: A multi-page science unit where each topic/organ/system follows the same template: draw-on-body-outline page → factual information pages → cloze fill-in-the-blank assessment with Word Box. Repeatable for ANY body system (digestive, circulatory, skeletal, muscular). The consistent template means the child can focus on content, not format.

notes: This connects to Carolyng's earlier drop of the Human Heart Mini Unit Study. Both users are showing human body content — Carolyng's was a more elaborate watercolor unit study with art integration, while Aless's is a simpler worksheet-style unit with a repeatable template. The draw-on-body-outline activity type is new and particularly good for spatial learning. The cloze-with-Word-Box pattern matches the Harcourt practice book format Carolyng showed (word bank + blanks). Both users converging on similar formats from different sources = strong validation.
